chunks: He (عليه السلام) was asked about the mud of rain that gets on the garment, in which there is urine, feces, and blood.
So he said: “Rain-soaked mud does not cause impurity.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or clothing affected by the mud
key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood, mentioned as a possible impurity present
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine, mentioned as a possible impurity present
key_terms.الْعَذِرَةُ: feces, mentioned as a possible impurity present
key_terms.الْمَطَرِ: rain; indicating the mud is mixed with rainwater
key_terms.طِينِ: mud or clay substance under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.يُنَجِّسُ: causes ritual impurity; renders something najis

ai.seo_question: Does rain-soaked mud on clothes make them najis if it may contain urine, feces, or blood?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on ritual purity regarding rain-soaked mud that may have contacted najasah. Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) states that such mud does not render clothing impure, indicating leniency in cases involving common outdoor exposure.
